patch_description: Replace the exponentially-weighted moving average with an adaptive 1D Kalman filter combined with a zero-phase forward/backward pass and trend-aware (constant-velocity) state model. A Kalman filter with a velocity state tracks trends better than any windowed average (drastically lower lag error), while adaptive measurement-noise estimation (via innovation-based noise floor tracking) suppresses spurious slope reversals and false reversals. The forward-backward (RTS-style smoothing) pass removes phase delay, improving responsiveness, correlation, and tracking accuracy while keeping O(N) complexity (efficiency stays high). The output length is kept identical to the original sliding-window output (len(x) - window_size + 1) for API compatibility, with outputs aligned to window centers so the alignment in run_signal_processing is correct (delay already accounted for there).
